FUNDAMENTALS OF MATERIALS SCIENCE: Basic knowledge of redox reactions
Relationship between microstructure and mechanical properties

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the level necessary to acquire the rest of the degree's competencies, including notions of the latest advances.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

Engineering analysis: The ability to analyze complex products, processes and systems in their field of study; choose and apply established analytical, calculation and experimental methods appropriately and correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Engineering analysis: The ability to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems in their specialty; choose and apply appropriate established analytical, calculation and experimental methods; recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial constraints.

Engineering projects: Ability to project, design and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes and systems in their specialty, which comply with established requirements, including being aware of social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate project methods.
Engineering projects: Project ability using advanced knowledge of their engineering specialty.

Research and innovation: Ability to perform bibliographic searches, consult and critically use databases and other information sources, to carry out simulation and analysis with the aim of conducting research on technical topics in their specialty.
Research and innovation: Ability to consult and apply good practice and safety codes in their specialty.
Research and innovation: Ability and skill to design and carry out experimental research, interpret results and draw conclusions in their field of study.
Practical application of engineering: Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, project and research and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Practical competence to solve complex problems, carry out complex engineering projects and conduct research specific to their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology and engineering processes and their limitations in the scope of their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial implications of engineering practice.
Judgment formulation: Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.

Communication and Teamwork: Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with engineers as well as people from other disciplines.
Continuous training: Ability to recognize the need for one's own continuous training and to undertake this activity throughout one's professional life independently.
Continuous training: Ability to keep up to date with new developments in science and technology.
Define the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, arguing and justifying each of them, and making correct use of language, in writing.
Knowledge and abilities for the application of materials engineering.

Ability to draft, sign and develop projects in the field of mechanical engineering whose object is the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacture, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants and manufacturing and automation processes.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, that enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of mechanical engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Ability to practice their profession with a cooperative and participatory attitude, and with social responsibility.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
That students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
That students have developed the necessary learning skills to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.

teaching_methods: Development, drafting and presentation of reports, memos, audiovisual material, etc., related to projects/POPBLs, carried out individually or in teams
Individual study and work, tests, exams and/or control points
Professor's presentation in the classroom, in participatory classes, of concepts and procedures associated with the subjects
Visits to laboratories, companies and/or CCTT
Computer simulation practices, individually and/or in teams
Resolution and realization of exercises, problems and practices individually and in teams

assessment_methods.method: Technical ability, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, documentation delivered, technical presentation and defense
Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Observation of student participation and attitude in the proposed training activities
Team oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject
Reports on the completion of exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices and laboratory practices

assessment_rules: Continuous evaluation and project feedback are used. Assessments often include technical ability, project involvement, work performed, results, documentation, and technical presentation and defense. Written and oral tests are common, with specific weightings for multiple exams (e.g., 25% for the first and 75% for the second for RGM331 and RGM332). Recovery mechanisms generally involve similar written or oral tests for technical competencies, though for some outcomes, no specific recovery is detailed.
